title: Approximation from an Exact-One Distinguisher
statement: Let an encoded maximization problem admit a one-one restriction search, and let a polynomial-time map distinguish its exact-one promise, outputting true on every valid instance with optimum $1$ and false on every valid instance with optimum less than $1$. Then the solution reconstructed from that map is feasible on every valid instance; moreover, it has value at least $1$ whenever the instance's optimum is at least $1$.
hypotheses_covered: The encoded maximization problem admits a one-one restriction search
The decision map is a polynomial-time map
The decision map distinguishes the exact-one promise
replaced:
Let an encoded maximization problem admit a one-one restriction search, and let a
polynomial-time decision map distinguish its exact-one promise: it outputs true on every
valid instance with optimum $1$ and false on every valid instance with optimum less than
$1$. Then the solution reconstructed from that decision map is feasible on every valid
instance, and whenever the optimum is at least $1$, its value is at least $1$.
